01.file

HIGH1▾

Vulnerability description

Credentials stored in an insecure file — SharedPreferences-derived sensitive data reaches a file write

Remediation

Canonicalize and validate every externally-influenced path before file access (File.getCanonicalPath + prefix check against a trusted base directory). Reject traversal sequences, use app-internal storage for sensitive files, and never delete or overwrite files outside the intended directory based on untrusted names.

CWE · References

CWE-22Path Traversal — developer.android.com ↗

02.ui-input

LOW1▾

Vulnerability description

Text from an editable UI field reaches a persistence write (SharedPreferences.Editor)

Remediation

Treat user-typed input as tainted end-to-end: sanitize or allow-list it before embedding into URLs, WebView loads, SQL, or network requests, and never relay raw typed input into privileged APIs.

CWE · References

CWE-79Www Project Mobile Top 10 — owasp.org ↗

03.webview

HIGH2▾

Vulnerability description

Attacker-controlled content is loaded into a WebView with JavaScript enabled — the page can execute attacker-controlled scripts (Unsafe WebView URL navigation)

Remediation

Do not load attacker-controlled URLs or content into a WebView. Restrict loadUrl/postUrl inputs to an allow-list of trusted origins, disable JavaScript and file access (setAllowFileAccess, setAllowFileAccessFromFileURLs, setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs) unless strictly required, and avoid exposing @JavascriptInterface bridges to untrusted content.

CWE · References

CWE-79Android Security Checklist Webview — oversecured.com ↗

04.sms

MEDIUM1▾

Vulnerability description

Attacker-controlled data reaches SmsManager.send* (premium-SMS / SMS injection)

Remediation

Never log credentials, auth tokens, device identifiers, location or other sensitive values. Strip sensitive fields before logging, use release-time log stripping, and ensure logs do not leak PII (CWE-532: insertion of sensitive information into log files).

05.logging

LOW1▾

Vulnerability description

Sensitive data leaked to log — data read from a database cursor or file reader reaches Log.* (CWE-532)

Remediation

Never log credentials, auth tokens, device identifiers, location or other sensitive values. Strip sensitive fields before logging, use release-time log stripping, and ensure logs do not leak PII (CWE-532: insertion of sensitive information into log files).

06.external-storage

HIGH2▾

Vulnerability description

A path derived from an external-storage directory File reaches a file write (Environment.getExternalStorage*/getExternalFilesDir flows)

Remediation

Treat shared/external storage as untrusted: do not load executable or plugin code from it, verify APK integrity before any dynamic load, and scope read/write access with scoped-storage APIs rather than broad legacy permissions.

CWE · References

CWE-276Sensitive Data External Storage — developer.android.com ↗
